plugin.name: iki/core
plugin.title: Core
plugin.description: The types every Iki deployment has.

iki/core.Alignment.name: Alignment
iki/core.Alignment.label: Alignment
iki/core.Alignment.description: Sequences aligned, as aligned FASTA, with the ones in Iki linked.

reference.name: reference
reference.label: Reference
reference.description: The sequence the others were aligned to, such as the plasmid a construct should be, or a reference protein.

members.name: members
members.label: Sequences
members.description: The sequences in Iki that it aligns: each is the row headed by its HRID. Rows that aren't sequences in Iki, such as reads, aren't listed.

aligned.name: aligned
aligned.label: Aligned sequences
aligned.description: The alignment as FASTA, a record per row with gaps as -: a sequence in Iki is headed by its HRID, anything else by its own name.

method.name: method
method.label: Method
method.description: How it was aligned, such as MAFFT 7.526 (--auto).

iki/core.App.name: App
iki/core.App.label: App
iki/core.App.description: A page of Iki's own components, each panel bound to those before it by expressions.

spec.name: spec
spec.label: Spec
spec.description: Its panels, in order (app/v1). Each is one of Iki's components, or an installed plugin's by its name (`acme/lab.box_map`), with its props and its width on a twelve-column grid. A prop that takes text or an entity can hold expressions between {{ and }}, which read the panels before it by their IDs: an entities grid offers `rows` and `selection`, a viewer `entity`, a plugin's component that lets people pick its `selection`. An app about an entity of a type (`entity.type`) is a tab on their pages in its project, and its expressions read that one as `entity`; a grid's conditions can then hold expressions too.

iki/core.Collection.name: Collection
iki/core.Collection.label: Collection
iki/core.Collection.description: A named set of entities, listed one by one or found by a search.

members.name: members
members.label: Members
members.description: The entities in a static collection, in order.

search.name: search
search.label: Search
search.description: What a dynamic collection holds: a search, as POST /entities/search takes it, without paging. It runs as whoever reads the collection.

iki/core.Sequence.name: Sequence
iki/core.Sequence.label: Sequence
iki/core.Sequence.description: Anything with a sequence of residues, such as DNA or a protein.

iki/core.View.name: View
iki/core.View.label: View
iki/core.View.description: A saved look at entities in Iki's viewers, each at the revision it showed.

target.name: target
target.label: Target
target.description: The entity it showed, before a view could show several.

target_revision.name: target_revision
target_revision.label: Revision
target_revision.description: The revision of the entity it showed, before a view could show several.

viewer.name: viewer
viewer.label: Viewer
viewer.description: The viewer it showed it in, before a view could show several.

targets.name: targets
targets.label: Entities
targets.description: The entities it shows, in order.

target_revisions.name: target_revisions
target_revisions.label: Revisions
target_revisions.description: The revision of each entity it shows, in the same order.

viewers.name: viewers
viewers.label: Viewers
viewers.description: Which of Iki's viewers shows each entity, in the same order, as the entity's type configures them. Entities in the structure viewer are drawn together, in one Mol* scene; each other one has a viewer of its own.

state.name: state
state.label: State
state.description: What the viewers showed, as they save it. `version` says which shape it is, so older views keep opening. Version 2 has `targets`, one for each entity in order: for the sequence viewer, the feature it showed; for the alignment viewer, the first column and row it showed; for the structure viewer, its colour, whether it's hidden, how it was moved to superpose it on another, and the residues selected. `camera` is where the structure viewer's camera was. Version 1 is a view of one entity, with its `feature`, `camera` or `position`.

transform.description: How it was moved, as a 4×4 matrix in column-major order, as Mol* keeps it.

superposed.description: What it was superposed on (the index of another entity in the structure viewer), and how closely: the RMSD in ångströms over the residues paired.

selection.description: The residues selected, as ranges of each chain's author numbering.
